title: Boundary geometry and buffer convention
current_behaviour: Cropland and pasture branches remain unknown without a supplied boundary zone. Grassland also needs managed_pasture_present.
definition: A zone beside real field boundaries where windbreak placement can be scoped. A classified grassland/cropland pixel is not a field boundary.
evidence_limit: Castle uses 10 m buffers in US Midwest. Pete approved variable regional width, not a universal 10 m. Contour buffers remain outside this gate.
datasets: [["USDA Crop Sequence Boundaries", "https://data.nass.usda.gov/Research_and_Science/Crop-Sequence-Boundaries/", "Estimated field polygons for contiguous US; reference implementation, not an Africa-wide input."], ["Local parcel or validated field-delineation layer", "", "Candidate only: pilot coverage, rights, age and accuracy still to establish."]]
recommended_action: Keep boundary geometry required; treat width as regional configuration. Agent searches coverage once pilot AOI known.
proposed_rule: Use validated field polygons/lines, buffer in projected metres using a documented width and convention (total width or width on each side). Remove duplicate shared edges. Report unique line length; buffered zone is applicability, not planted area. No numeric width selected here.
fallback: No geometry: unknown for this family, with a gap flag. Do not invent boundaries from coarse land-cover pixels.
exact_question: Accept geometry-first approach, with width deferred to regional evidence and no global default?
answer_options: ["Accept proposed approach", "Specify a regional width/source", "Keep current upload-only handling", "Defer"]
implementation_owner: Agent: source search, geometry QA, implementation. Pete: policy/region-specific width if known.
user_information: Pilot country/AOI; known boundary source if any. Optional width evidence, metres, and total-versus-each-side convention.

title: Grazing: measured condition or scoping proxy?
current_behaviour: Only WorldCover grassland (30) enters this branch; missing grazing mask makes it unknown.
definition: Grassland used by grazing livestock; not merely livestock somewhere in a coarse grid cell.
evidence_limit: Castle requires grazing animals but supplies no globally transferable livestock-density cutoff. Pete suggested GPW and GLW4; this card asks about the actual proxy rule.
datasets: [["GPW dominant grassland class", "https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_global-pasture-watch_assets_ggc-30m_v1_grassland_c", "30 m, cultivated and natural/semi-natural classes; no direct grazing measurement."], ["FAO GLW4", "https://www.fao.org/livestock-systems/global-distributions/en/", "2020 modelled livestock distribution; housed animals and mobile herds limit inference."]]
recommended_action: Allow a separately flagged scoping-proxy scenario; retain locally confirmed management as preferred input.
proposed_rule: Candidate scenario: grassland (GPW class 1 OR 2) AND any positive cattle/buffalo/goat/sheep density in GLW4. >0 means modelled presence, not a validated suitability cutoff. Keep native coarse livestock support visible. Missing either input remains unknown. Test extent and sensitivity before adopting as default. GPW versus current WorldCover extent must be compared explicitly.
fallback: Without proxy approval or local confirmation: retain unknown. Zero density must not prove non-grazing when model coverage is uncertain.
exact_question: Authorize GPW grassland + positive GLW4 ruminants as a flagged trial scenario, not a confirmed default?
answer_options: ["Approve flagged proxy trial", "Require local confirmation only", "Revise proxy rule", "Defer"]
implementation_owner: Agent: construct and compare masks, report uncertainty. Pete: accept or reject proxy policy.
user_information: Pilot AOI/year; known livestock-management survey if available. No personal dataset upload required to approve a trial.

title: Pasture management for boundary planting
current_behaviour: Cropland boundary branch does not need this mask; grassland boundary branch does.
definition: Pasture managed as part of an agricultural host system, including managed semi-natural grassland; not all natural grassland is pasture.
evidence_limit: Source says pasture/grassland. Additional management requirement is a conservative crosswalk choice; source does not prescribe a global managed-pasture classifier.
datasets: [["GPW + GLW4", "https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_global-pasture-watch_assets_ggc-30m_v1_grassland_c", "Same supporting layers as G1; cultivated grassland may be ungrazed forage."], ["Local pasture/land-use inventory", "", "Candidate, not acquired."]]
recommended_action: Reuse approved G1 proxy policy for a trial, avoiding a second independently invented classifier.
proposed_rule: If G1 trial approved: reuse its grassland/grazing candidate for this branch, then require field-boundary geometry. GPW cultivated class alone is insufficient. Confirmed pasture can override proxy. G2 cannot authorize G1 implicitly.
fallback: If no local confirmation and G1 not approved: grassland branch remains unknown; cropland boundary branch can still run.
exact_question: Reuse G1 flagged proxy for boundary grassland branch, conditional on separate G1 approval?
answer_options: ["Reuse G1 conditionally", "Require local pasture confirmation", "Revise definition", "Defer"]
implementation_owner: Agent: reuse mask and report inherited limitations. Pete: decide acceptable transfer.
user_information: No extra upload if G1 trial selected; local pasture inventory optional.

title: Ungrazed forage: limited silvoarable branch
current_behaviour: WorldCover cropland (40) already passes host gate; only grassland (30) needs this mask.
definition: Forage grown between planted tree rows without grazing animals: e.g. cut-and-carry or harvested fodder.
evidence_limit: Castle explicitly distinguishes ungrazed forage from silvopasture. GPW cannot establish absence of grazing; zero modelled livestock is not proof.
datasets: [["Local forage-use or farm-management map", "", "Preferred, but not acquired."], ["GPW", "https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_global-pasture-watch_assets_ggc-30m_v1_grassland_c", "Can locate candidate managed grassland, not confirm ungrazed use."]]
recommended_action: Keep this optional branch local-data dependent; do not block ordinary cropland silvoarable execution.
proposed_rule: Pass grassland only where a documented management input confirms forage without grazing. No automatic GPW/GLW4 absence inference.
fallback: Unknown for unsupported grassland branch; cropland continues. Grazed systems route to silvopastoral.
exact_question: Keep ungrazed-forage branch conditional on local confirmation, while proceeding on cropland?
answer_options: ["Accept limited branch", "Propose another evidence-backed proxy", "Defer grassland branch entirely", "Defer"]
implementation_owner: Agent: retain branch-specific gap flag. Pete: confirm acceptable scope.
user_information: Only supply management data if this branch matters in pilot; otherwise no action needed.

title: FMNR on cropland: is depletion a prerequisite?
current_behaviour: Cropland cannot pass current gate without depletion mask.
definition: Source describes improving depleted farmland; no operational definition of depletion is encoded.
evidence_limit: Single Kenyan WOCAT applicability statement; no threshold, time window, classifier or claim that non-depleted cropland is unsuitable. Hard gate is stronger than quoted evidence.
datasets: [["Local soil/farm condition assessment", "", "Could characterize depletion if definition and sampling support are supplied."], ["UNCCD land-degradation guidance", "https://www.unccd.int/resources/unccd-library/good-practice-guidance-sustainable-development-goal-sdg-indicator-1531", "Uses land cover, productivity and soil organic carbon; regional degradation does not directly define farm nutrient depletion."]]
recommended_action: Remove depletion as a universal hard eligibility requirement; retain it as restoration-targeting context. This is a proposed T4 change, not yet applied.
proposed_rule: Allow existing cropland as host context; attach depleted/unknown condition as descriptor where available. Do not infer actual FMNR establishment success. Rootstock and enabling conditions stay in their agreed operational/M6 route. Do not substitute low SOC or low NDVI as an unvalidated cutoff.
fallback: Until decision: current mask remains unknown. If proposed change approved: missing depletion data would no longer exclude/withhold cropland host eligibility.
exact_question: Remove universal depleted_farmland gate and retain depletion as restoration-targeting context?
answer_options: ["Approve moving depletion to context", "Keep hard gate and provide definition", "Request more evidence before changing", "Defer"]
implementation_owner: Agent: revise schema only after decision; identify context indicators. Pete: methodological gate-versus-context decision.
user_information: No raster required to answer this policy question. If retaining gate, specify indicator, reference period and defensible cutoff/source.

title: FMNR outside cropland: degradation versus farmland identity
current_behaviour: WorldCover grassland (30), shrubland (20) and bare/sparse (60) require degraded_farmland.
definition: Land independently identified as agricultural/fallow/former farmland suitable for the family context, with degradation separately characterized. Bare/shrub/grass cover alone cannot establish this.
evidence_limit: WOCAT describes degraded wasteland but gives no class-to-farmland crosswalk or universal degradation threshold. Natural grasslands/shrublands must not become restoration targets by default.
datasets: [["Local land-use history / restoration plan", "", "Preferred for farmland identity; not acquired."], ["UNCCD land-degradation guidance", "https://www.unccd.int/resources/unccd-library/good-practice-guidance-sustainable-development-goal-sdg-indicator-1531", "Possible condition descriptor; not evidence of farmland identity or FMNR suitability."]]
recommended_action: Replace ambiguous degradation gate with explicit farmland-context requirement; treat degradation as targeting context. Keep these branches unknown until farmland identity can be established.
proposed_rule: For grass/shrub/bare classes, require validated agricultural/fallow/former-farmland context. Degradation flag may characterize restoration need but cannot establish host identity. No automatic opening of natural ecosystems. Rootstock remains separately routed.
fallback: No farmland context: unknown, even if degradation product flags the pixel. Cropland branch follows separate D1 decision.
exact_question: Separate farmland identity from degradation, retaining a hard context check for non-cropland branches?
answer_options: ["Approve separated context requirement", "Keep current gate and define both components", "Request more evidence", "Defer"]
implementation_owner: Agent: locate land-use history inputs; implement separated condition after approval. Pete: confirm scope safeguard.
user_information: No immediate upload required; pilot AOI needed for source search. If known, identify local fallow/farmland or restoration inventory.

title: Crop hosts: approved fallback, optional local refinement
current_behaviour: OR crop gates and MapSPAM fractions already approved. Sources/bands configured; no AOI processed.
definition: Fraction of pixel occupied by supported crop; host extent, not shade benefit, shade deficit or suitability strength.
evidence_limit: Jezeer supports coffee/cocoa shaded-system identity. Tea is Pete-approved design scope, not evidence from that paper. Other crops need explicit configured scope.
datasets: [["MapSPAM 2020 v2r2", "https://cgiar-climate-data-hub.github.io/catalog/spam2020/", "Physical area ha: Arabica + Robusta, cocoa, tea; divide by native pixel area."], ["Accurate local commodity map", "", "Preferred where independently validated; not yet selected."]]
recommended_action: Proceed with already-approved MapSPAM fallback once AOI chosen. Treat local map request as optional refinement, not a new approval blocker.
proposed_rule: OR across positive crop fractions; preserve crop identities and fractions. Unknown components remain unknown where no other crop passes. Do not add duplicate technology totals or count whole coarse pixels as crop area. Local overrides need compatible units/provenance.
fallback: MapSPAM remains usable if no better map is supplied. Existing SLE upload preference does not block fallback.
exact_question: Any known local commodity map to assess, or proceed with approved fallback?
answer_options: ["Proceed with existing approval", "Assess local map named in notes", "Defer AOI run"]
implementation_owner: Agent: source acquisition, normalization and QA. Pete: AOI and optional local source knowledge.
user_information: Pilot country/AOI. Optional commodity-map link, year, crop classes and known limitations.
